newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end at highs in wake of Btp futures.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end at highs in wake of Btp futures.

text.p: Italian stock prices surged on Wednesday, ending at session highs, in the wake of soaring Btp bond futures betting all on European convergence and a narrowing of the spread over German bunds.
The Mib30 blue chip index ended 1.98 percent firmer at a record high of 19,612 while the all-share Mibtel index closed 1.67 percent up at 12,930, just off a session high at 12,931.
The June contract of the Fib30 bourse futures index also closed at a record high at 19,670 ahead of the expiry of future and options on Friday.
"We saw a fairly lifeless market until Btps started to climb," one dealer said. "Then the buying started, including foreign orders, on all the major blue chip stocks."

The September futures contract on the Italian Btp on LIFFE hit a new record peak at 133.15 in late European trade while the spread over the benchmark 10-year bund also narrowed to a record level of 124 basis points.

ENI rose 1.27 percent to 9,334 lire, Pirelli SpA rose 2.99 percent to 4,140, Benetton put on 3.76 percent to 26,523 and in telecoms, Stet holding gained 4.14 percent to 9,573 and Telecom Italia rose 3.87 percent to 5,210 ahead of their merger.
Dealers noted a block trade of 12.1 million Stet savings shares at 5,730 lire.
Olivetti faded on gloomy news from the groups AGM, ending 0.6 percent lower at 462.5 lire. Carlo De Benedetti's industrial holding Cir fell 0.93 percent to 1,065.
Fiat, which hit a year's high of 6,195 lire on Tuesday after upbeat prospects from the annual meeting, ended 0.95 percent up at 6,136 lire.
In banks, Credito Italiano put on 4.5 percent to 2,994 lire on a new buying wave.
Total traded volume was estimated at around 1.1 trillion lire, around the level of the previous session.
